findings.title: HEAD carried a committed file with unresolved git conflict markers
findings.location: apps/api/src/common/core/guards/authorization.guard.ts, landed via one of the two unlabelled 'update' commits (a77fa1f, 68c9f6e) on 2026-08-25
findings.impact: authorization.guard.ts as committed is not valid TypeScript (literal <<<<<<< / ||||||| / ======= / >>>>>>> markers). A fresh clone or CI checkout of main fails typecheck/build immediately. Root cause: an autostash (git stash list still shows stash@{0}) was popped mid-refactor, conflicted across ~17 files, and the manual resolution was left uncommitted (and in this one file, unstaged) while other touched files were committed as-is.
findings.evidence_detail: git show HEAD:apps/api/src/common/core/guards/authorization.guard.ts showed the raw markers; the working tree already carried a correct hand-resolved version, unstaged.
findings.note: Fixing this required finishing the refactor the conflict was in the middle of: consolidating the old apps/api/src/common/auth.ts barrel and the duplicate apps/api/src/common/guards/access-token.guard.ts into apps/api/src/common/core (which already held the canonical, current guard implementations - JWT algorithm pinned, TokenRevocationService-integrated AccessGuard), and wiring the previously-orphaned common/decorators/{authorize,public-rate-limit}.decorator.ts and common/utils/{assertion,runtime-environment}.util.ts into the common/core barrel so every module import resolves through one path. All ~17 affected files' imports verified consistent (no stale common/auth or common/errors references remain); full verify gate re-run clean: typecheck (api/web/contracts), lint (api/web), test (38 api suites/210 tests + 7 web suites/24 tests, 234 total), build (contracts/api/web) all green. A stale, unrelated autostash (stash@{0}) predating the common/core restructure and the commerce module split (diffs against apps/api/src/common/guards/authorization.guard.ts and commerce/commerce.controller.ts, paths that no longer exist) was left untouched rather than dropped or applied - flagged for the user to review.

findings.title: roles.manage lets a non-ADMIN grant FINANCE-level and other high-impact capability it does not itself hold
findings.location: apps/api/src/modules/admin/admin.service.ts setUserRoles (:177-215), assignRole (:241-257), grantPermission (:282-304); reached via PATCH /admin/users/:id/roles, POST /admin/roles, POST /admin/permissions/grant
findings.impact: A STAFF-tier actor holding only roles.manage can grant any other non-ADMIN role (FINANCE, STAFF, EXAMINER, SUPPORT, TEACHER) and any existing permission (payments.refund, payouts.manage, settings.manage, roles.manage itself) to another account without holding it themselves - only the literal ADMIN role is specially guarded (assertActorIsAdminToGrantAdmin). Real under current seed data: prisma/seed.ts:169 grants every permission key, including roles.manage, to the STAFF/SUPPORT/FINANCE/EXAMINER seed accounts alike.
findings.evidence: Read admin.service.ts in full; grantPermission validates the target permission key exists (admin.service.ts:285-286) but never checks the actor holds it or the target role; confirmed via prisma/seed.ts:111-176 that STAFF holds roles.manage by default
findings.fix: Added apps/api/src/modules/admin/role-management.policy.ts (RoleManagementPolicy: tier-1 ADMIN, tier-2 PRIVILEGED_ROLES=[FINANCE]/ELEVATED_PERMISSIONS=[roles.manage,payments.refund,payouts.manage,settings.manage] require actor already holds ADMIN, tier-3 everything else unchanged). Wired into admin.service.ts's createUser/setUserRoles/assignRole/grantPermission. Full policy documented in ROLE_MANAGEMENT_POLICY.md.
findings.regression_tests: apps/api/src/modules/admin/role-management.policy.spec.ts (policy unit tests, all tiers) + apps/api/src/modules/admin/admin.service.spec.ts describe('AdminService role-management hierarchy (SEC-207)') - the 4 required scenarios (STAFF cannot grant FINANCE; SUPPORT cannot grant payments.refund; FINANCE cannot grant roles.manage; ADMIN can perform allowed operations) plus a tier-3-unchanged regression and the full exploit-chain regression
findings.gates: typecheck (api/web/contracts)/lint (api/web)/build (contracts/api/web) green; unit+security-regression suite 235/235 (api) + 24/24 (web). Full e2e (test:e2e -w @lingospeak/api) has one pre-existing, unrelated failure (platform.e2e-spec.ts 'exposes admin operations...', shared student token revoked by an earlier assignRole call in the same test file, independently reproduced against the pre-SEC-207 code via git stash) - not caused by this fix, not fixed here (out of scope, different bug).

findings.title: Generic staff search endpoint exposes payment and role data to roles that don't need it
findings.impact: EXAMINER and SUPPORT roles can query GET /search/payments (amounts, status, payer name/phone) and GET /search/roles (role/permission assignments) despite neither role needing that data for its function - a least-privilege gap, not IDOR (all callers are legitimately authenticated staff).
findings.fix: Added apps/api/src/modules/search/search-access.policy.ts (SEARCH_ENTITY_PERMISSIONS map + assertMaySearch, fail-closed on unknown entity via SEARCH_ENTITY_INVALID, 403 SEARCH_PERMISSION_REQUIRED when the entity's mapped permission is absent). Wired into search.controller.ts via @CurrentUser() before delegating to SearchService; @Roles(...) class decorator kept unchanged as the coarse staff-tier gate. No new permission keys - every mapped permission already gates an equivalent /admin/* or /support/* endpoint.
findings.regression_tests: apps/api/src/modules/search/search-access.policy.spec.ts (pure policy unit tests, every entity x present/absent permission, unknown entity) + apps/api/src/modules/search/search.controller.spec.ts (the 5 required scenarios: SUPPORT cannot search payments; EXAMINER cannot search payments; SUPPORT cannot search roles; FINANCE can search payments with the permission; ADMIN can access all mapped entities - plus unknown-entity and SUPPORT-can-still-search-support-agents checks)
findings.gates: typecheck (api/web/contracts)/lint (api/web)/build (contracts/api/web) green; unit+security-regression suite 262/262 (api, up from 235) + 24/24 (web)
findings.remaining_risk: prisma/seed.ts still grants every permission key to every staff-tier seed account (ADMIN/STAFF/SUPPORT/FINANCE/EXAMINER alike), so the seeded/demo environment won't show a behavioural difference until seed data is separately tightened to least privilege - out of scope for this fix, tests use explicit minimal-permission fixtures instead of seed data to verify the mechanism independently.

findings.title: Refresh-token hash comparison is not constant-time
findings.impact: Inconsistent with the OTP path three lines away, which uses timingSafeEqual deliberately. Practical exploitability assessed as very low given SHA-256 avalanche (no smooth gradient for a timing attack to climb) and 256-bit secret entropy; flagged for defense-in-depth/consistency.
findings.fix: Added a shared constantTimeEqual(a,b) helper in auth.service.ts (Buffer length check + crypto.timingSafeEqual, avoids the throw-on-length-mismatch failure mode) and routed both the OTP code comparison (verifyOtp) and the refresh-token hash comparison (refresh) through it, replacing the plain hash(secret) !== session.tokenHash. No change to token format, session schema, rotation, family revocation, or cookie behaviour.
findings.regression_tests: apps/api/src/modules/auth/auth.service.spec.ts describe('AuthService.refresh (SEC-209)') - the 4 required scenarios (valid token succeeds; invalid/wrong-secret token rejected + family revoked; expired and separately revoked tokens rejected + family revoked; reuse detection still revokes the whole family) plus a malformed-token case and a buffer-length-mismatch safety case (the one scenario a plain !== could never exercise, since timingSafeEqual throws on unequal lengths rather than just returning false)

findings.title: Self-scoped route ownership checks are not covered by automated regression tests
findings.location: apps/api/src/authorization.spec.ts:94-121 SELF_SCOPED allowlist and the 42 services it references
findings.impact: authorization.spec.ts guarantees every route makes a deliberate access decision but does not runtime-verify the 42 SELF_SCOPED routes still filter by caller id - that rests on the one-time manual review in 02-security.md 2.2. A future regression in one of those services' ownership check would ship undetected.
findings.plan: AUDIT/SEC-210-coverage-plan.md - documents all 42 SELF_SCOPED routes, risk ranking, and which 4 got automated coverage this pass
findings.fix: Added ownership-boundary regression tests for the 4 highest-risk self-scoped route families (no production code changed for this finding): PaymentsService.gatewayRedirect (payments.service.spec.ts, extended - the existing gatewayRedirectHarness mock previously ignored its `where` args entirely, now mirrors real Prisma matching semantics), FilesService.download (files.service.spec.ts, new file - none existed before), SupportService.detail (support.workflow.spec.ts, extended), TestsService.resume (tests.service.resume.spec.ts, extended).
findings.regression_tests: 6 new/extended test cases across the 4 files above, each pairing a negative (different user denied) and positive (owner still succeeds) case per the task's 'do not test only successful owner access' requirement
findings.follow_up_noted_not_fixed: TestsService.resume() returns null (200 OK) rather than throwing notFound() for a non-owner, unlike the files/support/payments equivalents - not a data leak (no attempt data crosses the ownership boundary) but inconsistent response shape. Documented in SEC-210-coverage-plan.md as a candidate low-severity follow-up (working title SEC-211), not fixed here since changing resume()'s behaviour is outside 'add regression tests' scope and would need its own review cycle.

findings.title: TestsService.resume returns null instead of 404 for unauthorized ownership access
findings.location: apps/api/src/modules/tests/tests.service.ts resume(userId, id) - no notFound()/requireValue() wrapper around the findFirst result, unlike files.service.ts's download() and support.service.ts's detail()
findings.impact: GET /tests/attempts/:id returns 200 with a null body for a non-owner instead of a 404, inconsistent with the equivalent files/support/payments self-scoped routes. Not a data leak - no other user's attempt data is ever returned, confirmed by the SEC-210 regression test (TestsService.resume ownership (SEC-210) - 'returns nothing to a different user') - purely a response-shape/consistency issue.
findings.note: Surfaced while writing SEC-210 regression coverage. Deliberately not fixed: changing resume()'s behaviour to throw is outside 'add regression tests' scope and would need its own review cycle the way SEC-207/SEC-208 got. Regression test already pins the current (non-leaking) behaviour so a future fix has a green baseline to change against.

findings.title: Matching questionnaire computed availability for up to 40 teachers sequentially, with redundant per-teacher re-fetches
findings.impact: Root-caused as query elimination, not just sequential-vs-parallel: each candidate iteration re-fetched global settings (2 reads) and re-fetched the teacher row + availabilityRules the caller already had in memory, on top of genuinely per-teacher relation reads.
findings.fix: Added AvailabilityService.slotsForCandidates(): fetches global settings once and batches availabilityOverride/blockedPeriod/booking reads across all candidate teacherIds (teacherId: {in:[...]}) instead of once per candidate; extracted the pure slot-computation logic into a private computeSlots() helper shared with the unchanged single-teacher slots(). MatchingService.create() now calls it once instead of looping with await per teacher - the loop is no longer async at all, so no concurrency primitive was needed once the query elimination was done.
findings.evidence: Measured (not estimated) via Prisma query-event instrumentation against the live seeded DB: 84 SQL statements before (12 real candidates x 7 statements each) vs 5 statements after (constant, independent of candidate count) - a 94% reduction at N=12, improving further toward the endpoint's N=40 cap. Full e2e POST /api/matching test, followed by a real booking against a returned slot, both pass.
findings.regression_tests: matching.service.spec.ts (asserts slotsForCandidates called exactly once, not per-candidate); availability.service.spec.ts new 'AvailabilityService.slotsForCandidates (PERF-306)' describe block (per-candidate isolation + batched-query-count assertions)
findings.gates: typecheck/lint/build green; 281 api tests / 24 web tests; e2e 5/6 pass (the 1 failure is the pre-existing, unrelated TEST-001)

findings.title: No response compression
findings.impact: Every JSON response sent uncompressed - the broadest-reaching finding in the original report by surface area.
findings.fix: app.use(compression({ threshold: 1024 })) immediately after helmet(). Verified first: no StreamableFile/res.download/createReadStream/SSE anywhere in the API (files are served via presigned MinIO URLs, never streamed by the API itself); no reverse proxy/CDN in this repo already compressing, so no double-compression risk.
findings.evidence: Live-measured against the running dev server (auto-reloaded via nest start --watch): GET /api/languages 1864 -> 555 bytes (70.2%), GET /api/teachers?limit=12 10355 -> 1911 bytes (81.5%). npm ls postcss still resolves to the pinned 8.5.24 everywhere; npm audit shows the same pre-existing 5 advisories, zero new ones from the compression dependency.
findings.gates: typecheck/lint/build green; 281 api tests / 24 web tests

findings.title: Prisma issues one SQL statement per included to-many relation instead of a single joined query
findings.location: general - confirmed via apps/api/src/modules/bookings/availability.service.ts's teacher.findFirst include shape (4 to-many relations = 5 SQL statements, not 1)
findings.impact: Not specific to AvailabilityService - any service using include with multiple to-many relations pays this per-call cost. Blast radius across the codebase not sized this pass (would require its own grep/audit).
findings.note: Discovered while investigating PERF-306. Registered rather than fixed to avoid expanding Batch 1's approved scope. Recommended for Batch 2: evaluate Prisma's relationLoadStrategy: 'join' (PostgreSQL) as a global or per-query opt-in - a genuine architectural decision, not a drop-in fix.
